Did Anthony really hit Drury over the head with a petition?

Anthony's biographer, Elizabeth Cady Stanton, mentions this incident in her The Life and Work of Susan B. Anthony. A group of women had presented petitions to the New York State Assembly in Albany, asking that women be allowed to serve on juries, be appointed to public office, and be admitted to colleges and graduate schools. Anthony was there, probably as a representative of the New York State Woman Suffrage Association, which had also sent petitions on the same issue. Drury, who was against women's rights, had seen the petitions, and wanted them destroyed.
